key_findings.title: Zero-shot metric depth models improve cross‑domain generalization
key_findings.source: Survey on Monocular Metric Depth Estimation (arXiv:2501.11841v4)
key_findings.summary: Methods such as ZoeDepth (2023) and UniDepth (2024) combine relative‑depth pre‑training with adaptive metric binning or camera‑invariant modules, achieving strong performance on unseen datasets without finetuning.

key_findings.title: Adaptive depth binning (AdaBins, LocalBins, BinsFormer) yields finer discretisation and higher accuracy
key_findings.source: Survey on Monocular Metric Depth Estimation (arXiv:2501.11841v4)
key_findings.summary: Learning data‑dependent depth discretisation reduces quantisation error and is a common component in state‑of‑the‑art models from 2023‑2025.

key_findings.title: Attention‑enhanced multi‑scale fusion refines boundaries and thin structures
key_findings.source: Deep Learning‑based Depth Estimation Methods from Monocular Image and Videos: A Comprehensive Survey
key_findings.summary: Spatial, channel‑wise and hybrid attention mechanisms, combined with multi‑scale feature fusion, consistently improve depth fidelity, especially at object edges and for small or distant objects.

key_findings.title: Large‑scale semi‑supervised datasets are pivotal for zero‑shot performance
key_findings.source: Survey on Monocular Metric Depth Estimation (arXiv:2501.11841v4)
key_findings.summary: Depth Anything’s 62 M self‑annotated images and synthetic‑real hybrid data enable strong domain adaptation, demonstrating the importance of massive, diverse training corpora.

key_findings.title: Real‑time efficiency remains a bottleneck for detail‑preserving architectures
key_findings.source: Survey on Monocular Metric Depth Estimation (arXiv:2501.11841v4) & Towards Real-Time Monocular Depth Estimation for Robotics (2021)
key_findings.summary: Patch‑based and transformer‑based models (PatchFusion, BinsFormer) improve fine‑grained geometry but incur latency, while lightweight designs struggle to match their accuracy, highlighting an unresolved trade‑off.

synthesis: From 2023 to 2025 monocular depth estimation has shifted toward zero‑shot metric models that blend relative‑depth pre‑training with adaptive binning, enabling strong cross‑domain performance without explicit finetuning. Adaptive discretisation strategies such as AdaBins, LocalBins, and the transformer‑based BinsFormer have become standard, reducing quantisation error and boosting overall accuracy. Concurrently, attention‑enhanced multi‑scale fusion has emerged as a key technique for preserving sharp object boundaries and handling thin or distant structures, though its computational cost limits real‑time deployment. The explosion of large‑scale semi‑supervised datasets (e.g., Depth Anything’s 62 M self‑annotated images) and synthetic‑real hybrid pipelines has been instrumental in achieving these gains, yet models still exhibit geometric blurring and reduced fidelity on high‑resolution or out‑of‑distribution scenes. A persistent research gap lies in reconciling detail preservation with low latency, especially for robotics and AR/VR applications, and in establishing unified evaluation protocols that fairly compare metric versus relative depth outputs across diverse domains.
